problem_type: External CLI lifecycle and compatibility assumptions
symptom: Windows discovery is limited with an unknown version; newer media versions are rejected; handshake and drain failures mislead users.
direct_cause: Discovery gates Windows while prepared execution bypasses the gate; media uses exact version equality; hook command and discovery rely on shell/layout assumptions; handshake shares hook error; drain is fixed to text budget.
class_root: The CLI adapter lacks a single explicit platform, protocol-version and lifecycle policy plus exhaustive user-action diagnostics.

external_sources.purpose: Plugin-root hooks are also supported; user report only partially correct

invariants: Windows must not spawn until descendant ownership is proven, including prepared invocations.
Media compatibility is minimum-version based; actual capability and hook evidence remain required.
Hook discovery follows upstream customization layout; authorization markers remain in task-gate.
Drain and total runtime budgets derive from capability; no artifact returns before cleanup.
Each adapter error has an actionable translated diagnostic.
generality_proof: All discovery and execution paths share the platform guard; prepared and raw media validate the same version policy; all media stages share hook and drain ownership. The connection and model workspaces consume the same error mapping.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Reject unsupported platform before any input, identity or spawn; own process cleanup and capability drain.
Enforce minimum version for both raw and prepared media inputs.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Discovery calls platform guard before resolving environment or executable.
Direct and prepared execution both call guard before filesystem or spawn.
Prepared media records converge on assertAntigravityMediaInput.

recurrence.reason: Every Windows machine and future CLI media release can reach these shared assumptions.
same_class_scan: Inspected prepareAntigravity, runAntigravityProcess, assertPreparedAntigravityMediaInput, antigravityTask and both settings UI consumers.

prevention.invariant: Platform support is decided once and cannot be bypassed by executable preparation.
prevention.failure_mode: WINDOWS_UNSUPPORTED before spawn; protocol/hook failures withhold input and artifacts.
prevention.strategy: Use one platform guard in discovery and execution; preserve nonce authorization and minimum-version checks at shared media boundary.

legacy_paths.rationale: Remove prepared invocation platform bypass, exact media version gate, inline Windows shell assignment and plugin-root hooks copy.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: agy is user installed, not a pinned application dependency. Native Windows Job Object ownership is unavailable through Node built-ins; do not install a wrapper that cannot supply the guarantee.
dependency_lifecycle.current: Observed local agy 1.1.22; reported Windows 1.1.27; media evidence advanced to 1.1.22 by this live image run.
dependency_lifecycle.target: Minimum 1.1.21 with actual per-version capability verification; Windows support after lifecycle RC proof.
exit_criteria: Prove cancellation and early-parent-exit descendant cleanup on Windows RC using Node built-ins or a separately approved owned runtime.
Retire unsupported guard only once Windows lifecycle regression coverage and real RC evidence pass.

migration: No stored data migration. Temporary customization workspace is rebuilt per run; cached capability success remains exact-version bound.
residual_risks: Windows is explicitly unsupported; Windows 真机待群里那位用户用 RC 验。
CLI stream-json hook invocation on reported 1.1.27 remains unverified; loading a named hook does not prove execution.
